sections.text: The Trump administration paused plans to deport a group of more than 150 Afghans, after a temporary court order blocking their removal expired. Some detainees were moved to long-term facilities, leaving their departure dates unspecified.

sections.text: Human rights advocates and lawmakers warn that returning Afghans to Taliban rule poses severe dangers, including arbitrary detention, torture and execution. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Researchers analyzed twelve years of data on wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They discovered that when deaths and departures exceeded new arrivals, the elephant society fractured rather than simply shrinking. Relationships weakened as forage disappeared due to invasive plants and ecological changes.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Elephants typically possess resilient communities that survive occasional deaths. However, continuous losses erode social networks by removing key individuals and casual ties that connect different groups, leaving populations vulnerable to collapse.

sections.text: Eve Taylor was admitted to Ysbyty Gwynedd with signs of potential infection after her waters broke. A midwife decided not to wake her for scheduled monitoring.
